d.t: An utterance of oh; a spoken expression of surprise, acknowledgement, etc.
d.e: There were ohs and ahs, and the people twisted about as they looked for her. Then they began to applaud.

d.t: The name of the Latin script letter O/o.
d.e: One genuine recycled local glass of aitch-two-oh

d.t: The digit 0 (especially in representations of speech)
d.e: Jenny I've got your number. I need to make you mine. Jenny don't change your number. Eight six seven five three oh nine. Eight six seven five three oh nine. Eight six seven five three oh nine. Eight six seven five three oh nine. Tommy Tutone, "867-5309/Jenny"

d.t: Expression of surprise.
d.e: Oh! I didn't see you there.

d.t: Expression of wonder, amazement, or awe.
d.e: Oh, wow! That's amazing.

d.t: Expression of understanding, affirmation, recognition, or realization.
d.e: Oh, so that's how it works.

d.t: A word to precede an annoyed remark.
d.e: Oh, leave me alone.

d.t: A word to precede an added or offhand comment or afterthought.
d.e: Oh, and don't forget your coat.

d.t: An invocation or address (similar to the vocative in languages with noun declension), often with a term of endearment.
d.e: Oh, gosh.

d.t: Exclamation for drama or emphasis.
d.e: Oh, when will it end?

d.t: Expression of pain. See ouch.
d.e: Oh! That hurt.

d.t: To utter the interjection oh; to express surprise, etc.
d.e: A quarter of an hour elapsed, and then, after several rings at the door-bell, a smothered laugh, and a good deal of ohing and ahing, the door was thrown open, and one by one, as they were announced, in came the expected characters.

d.t: An expression of delight or joy.
d.e: Oh, boy! I can't wait to tell my friends about this!

d.t: An expression of dismay, resignation, frustration, or annoyance (sarcastic).
d.e: Oh, boy. This is going to be a lot of work.

d.t: A game or time period in which a player did not manage to sustain a particular attainment.
d.e: Jones has gone oh for on his scoring opportunities this season.

d.t: An instance in which a player did not get a hit in a game.
d.e: Yesterday's oh for made him overly aggressive today at the plate.

d.t: An expression of delight and joy, or, sarcastically, dismay, resignation, frustration, or annoyance.
d.e: Oh, girl! I can't wait to tell my friends about this!

d.t: A trick-taking card game of British origin in which the object is to take exactly the number of tricks bid.
Used to express disappointment or annoyance.
d.e: Oh, man, I wish we didn't have to clean up the whole house.

d.t: Used to express excitement or enthusiasm.
d.e: Oh, man, that was a great ride!

d.t: an expression of amazement
oh my God
d.e: Which might mean shaping it, gelling it, snooting it, barn dooring it, and putting it on a stand or a clamp. Maybe taking the dome diffuser off. Perhaps zooming it. Oh my. And you thought you were just taking a picture.

d.t: An exclamation of astonishment or gleeful disapproval.
d.e: “[…] Oh, my days, don’t ’ee say another word about either of ’em. I wish I’d never been born.”

d.t: Expression of shock or dismay.
An expression of anger, frustration, excitement, shock, dismay, etc.
d.e: Oh my God (Oh my fucking God)

d.t: Said in supplication to God.
An expression of anger, frustration, excitement, shock, awe, dismay, etc.
d.e: Creep niggas like a seal Tote the steel Stick a nigga, make him squeal "Oh, my God!" Those can't be the last words of ya man Damn, ya man was so hard

d.t: Expression of shock, frustration, or dismay.
d.e: Old strap for strop, penn’orth of emery powder, bit of Sunlight, nail‐brush to rub it on face, and — oh my hell !— torture — and your face is smooth again.

d.t: Synonym of oh my days.
An expression of surprise, astonishment, shock, dismay, supplication, or consternation.
d.e: "Oh my Lord!" said a stunned Geneva McNeil, reached by telephone at her East Baltimore home and told that the jury had awarded $3.3 million to her and her ailing husband.

d.t: An expression of surprise or astonishment.
d.e: “Oh my word ... Mr. Williams ... I am so sorry about before. I had no idea it was you.”

d.t: An exclamation or expression of alarm about a problem or error.
d.e: Oh, no! The rug is on fire!

d.t: An exclamation of surprise or amazement.
d.e: Well, one day when she got tired of my seemingly spaced-out replies she let me have it. She responded with, "Oh Mommy, I had a horrible day. First I lost my lunch pail and the teacher wouldn't let me go to the office for help. Then I got upset and jumped off the building." My…

d.t: Said in response to an obvious statement.
d.e: 'It's a sniper' shouted the bush. ‘Oh really! Did you hear that boys, it's a fucking sniper. What am I? Am I talking in Czechoslovakian or what? I know it's a fuckin' sniper.’

d.t: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see oh, really.
d.e: "In less than two hours Simon is picking me up, and we're going to Maui for the weekend." “Oh, really.” The line was silent for a moment. “And just what are his intentions in this romantic getaway?”

d.t: very, extremely (often ironic)
d.e: His oh-so-witty (ugh) remarks on the loud hailer constitute one more proof that this instrument has minimal value on a pleasure boat.

d.t: An expression of mild disappointment or resignation: too bad; it's a pity; what can you do; it is what it is.
d.e: I didn’t know the store closes at five on Thursdays. Oh well, I’ll have to come back tomorrow.

d.t: Used to indicate agreement, often sarcastically.
d.e: Are you going to the party? — Oh, yeah!

d.t: Used to introduce a refutation, sometimes sarcastically.
d.e: (In a poker game): I raise you twenty. — Oh, yeah? I think you're bluffing. I call.

d.t: An exclamation of excitement or joy.
d.e: Oh, yeah, I got a new video game!

d.t: Used when suddenly remembering something.
d.e: Oh, yeah, there was a police car outside the building for some reason.

d.t: An extended Hawaiian family unit.
d.e: [U]nder the leadership of Ka Lahui Hawai'i headed by attorney Mililani Trask, various Native Hawaiian organizations, ohanas, and individuals formed a loose coalition that some refer to as the Hawaiian Nation within a Nation.

d.t: A structure erected over the grave of a great and righteous person.
Either of two flowering trees of the myrtle family, especially
d.e: The dominant canopy plant is the Ohi‘a, a greyish tree of medium height, often gnarled and dressed with lichens, and carrying small, oval, dark green leaves that shine attractively in a certain light.

d.t: A native or resident of the state of Ohio in the United States of America.
d.e: Finally, it’s all over. I’m pretty sure that is what a lot of Ohioans are thinking. None of us has ever been through anything like this, and it was not pleasant. […] It does make some sense to have an Ohioan at the top of the ticket.

d.t: Pertaining to or from Ohio.
An instance of defeating an opponent with a single attack; a one-hit knockout.
To defeat with a single attack.
A member of an indigenous population native to the San Francisco and Monterey Bay Areas, California.
In the International System of Units, the derived unit of electrical resistance; the electrical resistance of a device across which a potential difference of one volt causes a current of one ampere.
d.e: If the volt, ampere and ohm were taken as the absolute units, the practical units would be the ampere, begohm and begavolt, names just as convenient as ampere, coulomb and farad.

d.t: Of or relating to, or measured in, ohms.
That obeys Ohm's law.
A portable device for measuring relatively small values of electrical resistance.
Expressing surprise or gloating realisation; aha.
d.e: "There is Kate, taking no heed of anybody; sensible old darling — she goes at her tea and cake — Oho! she has not touched them!"

d.t: The sound of weeping; boo-hoo.
d.e: "Oho, oho, oho!" she wailed. "I didn't know; I didn't know. I meant no harm; indeed I didn't, ma'am."

d.t: A kind of rural commune established in New Zealand under a government scheme of the mid-1970s.
Initialism of off-highway vehicle.
